Short answer: Yes — as of today (September 4, 2026) Ireland’s standard VAT rate is 23%, and electronically supplied (digital) services supplied to Irish consumers are taxed at that rate. ([revenue.ie](https://www.revenue.ie/en/vat/vat-rates/search-vat-rates/current-VAT-rates.aspx?utm_source=openai))

A few quick caveats to check before you send the PDF:
- If the buyer is outside Ireland (another EU country), EU place-of-supply rules generally require you to charge the customer’s local VAT rate for B2C digital services. ([taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu](https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/taxation/vat/vat-directive/vat-rates_en?utm_source=openai))  
- If the buyer is a VAT-registered business in another EU state and provides a valid VAT number, the supply may be treated as B2B (reverse charge) so you would not charge Irish VAT. See Revenue’s guidance on electronically supplied services for the registration/threshold rules. ([revenue.ie](https://www.revenue.ie/en/vat/vat-on-services/electronic-services/vat-and-electronically-supplied-services/index.aspx?utm_source=openai))
- Recent Irish Budget/2026 changes reduced some reduced VAT rates (e.g., certain hospitality items to 9% from July 1, 2026) but did not change the 23% standard rate. ([revenue.ie](https://www.revenue.ie/en/corporate/documents/statistics/ready-reckoner.pdf?utm_source=openai))

I couldn’t inspect your actual PDF (you didn’t attach it) — I relied on Revenue/EC sources above. If you tell me whether the client is in Ireland or is a VAT-registered business (and you can paste the exact wording from your pricing PDF if you want), I’ll give the exact wording you should use or a one-line update you can drop into the document.
